correctness.rationale: For product-of-chain order, two-variable nested chain formulas define exact element rank and total top rank. Every rank-one atom has maximal incomparable rank S-e_i, explicitly attained and characterizing its factor exponent. For each exponent e, a two-variable universal condition tests whether a rank-k vector is above every atom of type e. The least successful k is exactly the number of those coordinate atoms. This recovers all multiplicities; rank-zero singleton and one-factor chains are handled separately. Recursion, variable shadowing and all quantifier ranges are explicit. A 102-instance finite checker and independent syntactic two-variable formula evaluator corroborate the critical identities and sample separators, with no infinite extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The closest full texts concern C2 with counting, order-invariance of FO2 with extra named orders, and satisfiability of partial-order FO2 fragments. Searches of equivalent statements, broader results, databases and implication chains did not reveal the exact counting-free two-variable pure-divisibility classification for arbitrary finite products of chains. The possibility of a prior unstated corollary of a modal rigidity theorem remains a real but nondecisive priority risk.
residual_risks: The search is not exhaustive: an older modal-logic rigidity result for products of chains might already imply the theorem.
Finite-product counting-free logic could be covered under terminology not encountered, such as modal rank profiles or incomparability spectra.
Independent historical priority assessment has not been performed.

value.rationale: A natural infinite arithmetic family (all positive-integer divisor posets) has a complete relative FO2 theory classification, even though FO2 cannot count arbitrary same-type elements. The rank/incomparable-atom mechanism reconstructs multiplicities of each prime exponent and works with any number of factors. One variable is provably insufficient; ordinary finite lattices need not have this property. Equal-size/equal-height but distinguishable examples and same exponent support with different multiplicities show the structural content is not a cardinality or height observation.
